item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-21e696df6835a12f","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In March 2023, López Obrador said he was absolutely certain there was no conflict of interest involving his son José Ramón López Beltrán, but ordered an investigation or response to complaints, instructed Pemex's director to include the matter in a Baker Hughes-related report, and noted that the FGR had been asked to deliver his brother's case file to the INE. He also publicly rejected the allegations and accused a journalist of calumny.","question_ids":["7B.1","7B.2","7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly reported in March 2023; concerns events and official responses from 2022-2023.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the statements and investigative instructions to President Andrés Manuel López Obrador.","limitations":["The supplied units do not report the investigation's final findings, sanctions, recovery, or whether the review was institutionally independent."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b70badd8c86e0286","start_unit":1,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Mexico's 2022 NPT statement, issued by its permanent representative under López Obrador's government, reaffirmed reliance on international law rather than nuclear deterrence, highlighted Mexico's role in the Tlatelolco Treaty and support for the TPNW, endorsed full NPT implementation, the IAEA Additional Protocol, export controls, safeguards, nuclear-facility safety, and disarmament, and condemned nuclear threats and elevated operational alert during the Ukraine war.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.3","1B.4","1B.5","1B.6","1B.8","1B.10","2B.1","2B.3","2B.7","2B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Official policy position stated in August 2022 and relevant to Mexico's posture entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statement was delivered by Mexico's permanent representative and presents Mexico's official position during López Obrador's presidency.","limitations":["The units establish diplomatic commitments and rhetoric, but not their full domestic implementation, funding, or measurable effect in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2fea0530434a9be0","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The AIFA airport, inaugurated under López Obrador, was reported to have lost approximately 4.02 million pesos per operating day through December 2022 after subsidies, with operating expenses 9.2 times daily revenue; it handled 1.3 million passengers against a first-year target of 2.4 million, while management projected financial profitability if traffic reached 200 daily flights.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Reports 2022 performance in an article published March 2023, relevant to evaluation of the program at the start of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The airport was a flagship government project; the supplied text attributes operational targets and projections to AIFA's director and the government.","limitations":["The supplied units do not establish the full project cost, later 2023 performance, or whether corrective measures were adopted."]},{"source_id":"SRC-eee53242df59e70b","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL's 2023 results-oriented evaluation assesses whether social programs clearly define target populations and intended outcomes, use indicators to monitor results, and link delivered goods or services to their central objectives; it identifies improvement areas and provides a 2023 program database.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.5","6B.9","8B.1","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The evaluation framework and 2023 database are directly relevant to the 2023 social-program monitoring environment.","ruler_attribution":"CONEVAL is the independent evaluation institution; the supplied unit describes its evaluation system rather than a specific presidential decision.","limitations":["The supplied unit does not provide program-level findings or establish López Obrador's response to identified weaknesses."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a22c3163b858abf","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL's 2022-2023 integrated performance summary used monitoring and evaluation information for fiscal year 2022 and categorized 121 federal social programs and actions in a structured database for comparison and decision support.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.5","6B.9","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Covers fiscal-year 2022 performance and was available for assessment during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The evaluation was produced by CONEVAL for federal social programs under López Obrador's administration.","limitations":["The supplied units do not state the individual program results, distributional effects, or whether the administration implemented CONEVAL recommendations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1eb3b87b7c07ff6c","start_unit":16,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"International IDEA reported that López Obrador's proposed electoral reform would change appointment of electoral authorities so the president and ruling party could control most nominations, significantly cut the electoral authority's budget, and eliminate local electoral authorities. Civil society organized mass demonstrations over perceived risks to institutional independence and election integrity; he also announced a fallback statutory reform if the constitutional amendment lacked the required congressional majority.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.8","4B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report concerns November 2022 developments that shaped the political-freedom environment entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"International IDEA attributes the proposal and fallback plan to President Andrés Manuel López Obrador.","limitations":["The supplied units do not report the final legal status, implementation, judicial review, or subsequent correction of the reforms."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f52ddf0fc8fdfc0a","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Le Monde reported that López Obrador condemned Russia's invasion of Ukraine but refused to sanction Moscow, describing Mexico's position as neutrality; the stance strained relations with Washington, while members of his party created a Mexico-Russia friendship committee in Congress. A U.S. general alleged that Mexico hosted many Russian spies, an allegation the president neither denied nor confirmed in the supplied text.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.3","2B.5","2B.6","2B.7","2B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Reports March 2022 foreign-policy conduct relevant to the ruler's continuing international posture in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the neutrality policy to López Obrador and separately reports conduct by members of his party.","limitations":["The article is partly paywalled; the supplied units do not establish the complete diplomatic record, intelligence verification, or 2023 continuation of the policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7885b287c6f37bac","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"IMCO's 2023 Corruption Risk Index, covering 2022 federal spending, found increased corruption risk in 184 of 260 institutions, citing reduced competition, missing contract publications, and delayed Compranet registration. It reported 38% of spending through direct allocation, 51% published after the start date, 2.5 million pesos allocated to ghost businesses, 107.868 million to penalized businesses, and 3.474 billion to newly incorporated businesses; medicine procurement was 74% direct allocation.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.3","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published July 2023 and evaluates federal expenditures during 2022, directly informing 2023 governance assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern federal public administration under López Obrador's government; IMCO attributes risk to institutional spending practices rather than proving personal presidential involvement.","limitations":["The supplied units do not establish López Obrador's personal knowledge, direction, benefit, or response to each finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-de1098415dc558b8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Verificado examined 30 factual claims in López Obrador's Fourth Government Report and classified 9 as true, 8 as misleading, and 13 as false. It said the speech emphasized future promises and projects, often lacked context or source detail, and repeated claims about corruption, crime, economic stability, and other achievements that had previously been checked against government data and specialist evidence.","question_ids":["5B.7","6B.5","7B.1","7B.2","7B.8","7B.10","8B.1","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was delivered and fact-checked in September 2022; it is relevant as evidence of the communication and accountability posture entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The claims were made by President Andrés Manuel López Obrador in his Fourth Government Report.","limitations":["The supplied units summarize classifications without reproducing the underlying claim-by-claim evidence or documenting whether López Obrador corrected the statements."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d8f2f095cc25a764","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"An investigation reported that leaked SEDENA documents showed a secret Mexican Army intelligence unit used Pegasus spyware against human-rights defender Raymundo Ramos to access or interfere with investigations into alleged Army extrajudicial executions. The report said the Defense Ministry knew of the operation, that the surveillance of a civilian was illegal because the armed forces lacked authority to intercept private communications, and that no judicial authorization was recorded by the Federal Judiciary.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Reported March 2023 about surveillance conducted in August 2020, during López Obrador's administration, with implications for the 2023 accountability environment.","ruler_attribution":"The supplied report attributes the operation to a secret Army intelligence unit and states that the Defense Ministry knew; it does not establish that López Obrador personally ordered it.","limitations":["The source is a report relaying an investigation and explicitly disclaims independent verification; the supplied units do not state the president's personal knowledge, disciplinary action, judicial outcome, or remedy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0567a4cc8d45508e","start_unit":5,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"World Bank WITS reported Mexico's 2022 exports at US$577.731 billion and imports at US$604.615 billion, with trade equal to 88.83% of GDP, a trade balance of -US$43.038 billion, and exports to the United States representing 78.29% of total exports. It also reported GDP of US$1.466 trillion and country growth of 7.44% in the displayed trade indicators.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Reports national trade and macroeconomic indicators for 2022, useful as baseline context for 2023 evaluation.","ruler_attribution":"The data describe Mexico's economy during López Obrador's administration but do not attribute outcomes solely to presidential decisions.","limitations":["The supplied units provide aggregate indicators without causal attribution, distributional effects, policy counterfactuals, or 2023 outcomes."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["Several sources concern 2022 rather than 2023 and therefore provide entering-period or baseline evidence.","The supplied extracts frequently report institutional or policy-level facts without establishing López Obrador's personal knowledge, intent, or responsibility.","No scores are assigned; facts are mapped to potentially applicable questions without resolving the chapter judgments."]}
